description: Fictional NHS administrative logistics pilot; no patient data or clinical judgments.

sections.1_scope: A four-week pilot of supply-request routing in one fictional hospital store. The aim is to reduce staff administration and retain urgent manual escalation.
sections.2_method: The operations team timed 40 synthetic requests before and 40 during the pilot. Samples were not randomized; request mix may differ.
sections.3_results: Mean handling time was 12 minutes before and 9 minutes during the pilot. These are sample means, not evidence of system-wide savings.
sections.4_limits: Acquisition price, recurring software cost, implementation hours and downstream effects were not measured. No clinical outcomes were evaluated.
sections.5_safeguards: A human logistics coordinator reviews urgent flags. Wider rollout requires evaluation and governance approval.

notice.text: With effect from 1 November 2026, routine supply requisitions must be submitted through the new portal by 2pm for next-working-day processing. Urgent requirements remain subject to the existing telephone escalation procedure and must not be deferred pending portal processing. The four-week pilot involved one store only. Staff without portal access should contact the stores desk for assistance.
